question.prompt: What is the tens digit of \(6^{6^6}?\)

solutions.title: Track the last two digits
solutions.explanation:
The tens digit depends only on the last two digits, and those digits repeat quickly among powers of \(6\).

Starting with \(6^2=36\), multiply by \(6\) repeatedly and keep only the last two digits:

| Exponent \(n\) | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Last two digits of \(6^n\) | 36 | 16 | 96 | 76 | 56 | 36 |

Once \(36\) returns, the same sequence repeats, because each next pair of digits is determined by multiplying the previous pair by \(6\). Thus the cycle has length \(5\), starting at exponent \(2\).

Let \(N=6^6\), so the number in the question is \(6^N\). Since \(6\) leaves remainder \(1\) upon division by \(5\), so does every positive power of \(6\). Hence
\[
N\equiv1\pmod5.
\]
Here \(\equiv\) means that the two numbers have the same remainder. Since \(N>1\), it occupies the same position in the cycle as exponent \(6\), which also leaves remainder \(1\) upon division by \(5\).

Therefore \(6^N\) ends in \(56\), and its tens digit is \(\boxed{5}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutions.title: Combine two smaller remainders
solutions.explanation:
Because \(100=4\cdot25\), we can determine the last two digits by finding a remainder modulo \(25\) and checking divisibility by \(4\).

Let \(N=6^6\). Since \(6\equiv1\pmod5\), we have \(N\equiv1\pmod5\), so \(N=5k+1\) for an integer \(k\). Also,
\[
6^5=7776\equiv1\pmod{25}.
\]
Here congruence means equality of remainders. It follows that
\[
6^N=(6^5)^k\cdot6\equiv1^k\cdot6=6\pmod{25}.
\]
Since \(N\ge2\), the number \(6^N\) is divisible by \(4\).

Let \(d\) be the number formed by its last two digits, with \(0\le d\le99\). Removing a multiple of \(100\) preserves both conditions. The numbers in this range that leave remainder \(6\) modulo \(25\) are exactly
\[
6,\quad31,\quad56,\quad81.
\]
Only \(56\) is divisible by \(4\). Thus the last two digits are \(56\), and the tens digit is \(\boxed{5}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
